subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Arab Cryptanalysts
description: A 60-second lesson on The Arab Cryptanalysts.

hook.text: In the 9th century, an Arab scholar invented the technique that breaks almost every simple cipher.

buildup.text: Al-Kindi studied the Quran and noticed that certain letters appear far more often than others.

discovery.text: He invented frequency analysis: counting letter patterns to crack substitution ciphers.

twist.text: For 800 years after Al-Kindi, frequency analysis defeated every major cipher Europeans invented.

climax.text: One insight — that languages have patterns — broke centuries of codes and changed cryptography forever.

punchline.text: Count the letters. The code breaks itself.

quiz.question: What is frequency analysis in cryptography?
options: Counting letter patterns to reveal the original message
Measuring radio signal frequencies to intercept messages
Analyzing how often encrypted messages are sent
